items.headline: Flood Watch issued May 5 at 10:55AM AKDT until May 6 at 11:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by an ice jam is possible.

* WHERE...In Eagle and areas downstream

* WHEN...Through Wednesday morning.

* IMPACTS...Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The Yukon River has broken up locally at Eagle. As of 10 am
Tuesday breakup had not progressed to Calico Bluffs.  Water
levels remain low behind the ice front.  Ice shows signs of
weakening but the possibility of minor flooding exists if ice
jams form.

- Http://www.weather.gov/apr
items.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued May 5 at 8:01AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
As a front pushes across the Brooks Range, snow totals of around 4
to 7 inches will be possible across the Central Arctic Coast,
especially between Utqiagvik and Nuiqsut, and the Central Arctic
Plains. The highest snowfall rates are likely to occur from
Tuesday night through Wednesday afternoon. Along the Dalton

items.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued May 5 at 5:54AM AKDT until May 7 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
items.description:
* WHAT...Snow and blowing snow expected. Total snow accumulations
between 1 to 3 inches. Winds gusting as high as 45 mph.

* WHERE...Eastern Beaufort Sea Coast.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM AKDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Areas of blowing snow could
reduce visibility to as low as a half mile at times.
items.instruction: Slow down and use caution while traveling.

items.headline: Wind Advisory issued May 5 at 5:36AM AKDT until May 5 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
items.description:
* WHAT...South winds 20 to 30 mph with gusts up to 45 mph expected.

* WHERE...Municipality of Skagway.

* WHEN...From 1 PM this afternoon to 10 PM AKDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.
items.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

Secure outdoor objects.
